history.period: Modern (built by Shree Shyam Satsang Mandal, Ghusuridham)
history.summary: Khatu Shyam (Shyam Baba) temple at Ghusuri, Howrah, built by Shree Shyam Satsang Mandal, Ghusuridham with support of Shyam devotees in Kolkata. Described as the biggest Khatu Shyam temple in the eastern region of India. Located at 132 Jogendra Nath Mukherjee Road, Vivekanand Colony, Ghusuri, Howrah 711107. IDENTITY CONFIRMED (Wikipedia entry exists).

name: Shree Shyam Mandir, Ghusuri
town_description: Ghusuri is a neighbourhood in Howrah city, West Bengal, on the west bank of the Hooghly river opposite northern Kolkata. Part of the Greater Kolkata industrial belt, it is best known outside the city for the Ghusuri Dham Khatu Shyam temple.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~18 km)
travel.railway: Howrah station ~6 km; buses and autos via G.T. Road to Ghusuri (Jogendra Nath Mukherjee Road)
travel.road: At 132 Jogendra Nath Mukherjee Road, Ghusuri, Howrah 711107; accessible from Howrah and northern Kolkata via the Bally bridge / G.T. Road corridor.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Ekadashi days are busiest.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-1:00 PM and 4:00 PM-9:00 PM daily (closes 1:00 PM-4:00 PM). Aartis: Mangla 6:00 AM, Shringaar 8:30 AM, Bhog 11:30 AM, Sandhya 7:00 PM, Sayan 8:45 PM (per temple's social pages).
